detailed_description: SQL Query Optimizer performs a local static review of pasted SQL. Choose Generic SQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, or SQL Server; optionally paste EXPLAIN text; then review the score, formatted SQL, evidence excerpts, cautious findings, and composite index candidates. The analyzer never connects to a database, executes SQL, applies rewrites, verifies indexes, or guarantees a speed improvement. Local diagnostic explanations are in English.
usage_steps: Choose the database dialect that best matches the SQL.
Paste SQL and, if available, paste EXPLAIN text from your own database tool.
Select Analyze locally to run the browser-only static review.
Review each English diagnostic, its evidence excerpt, index candidates, formatted SQL, and limitations.
Copy only the material you need, then validate any change in your own database environment.
usage_examples: Review SELECT * and unbounded reads before code review.
Spot UPDATE or DELETE statements without a WHERE clause.
Inspect PostgreSQL Seq Scan, MySQL type: ALL, SQLite SCAN, or SQL Server Table Scan text that you paste.
Draft a composite index candidate from equality filters and ORDER BY columns, then verify it against the real schema and workload.

faqs.question: Does this connect to or run queries on my database?
faqs.answer: No. The browser tool analyzes only the SQL and optional EXPLAIN text you paste. It does not connect to a database or execute SQL.

faqs.question: Does it rewrite my query automatically?
faqs.answer: No. It provides formatted SQL and review findings but never applies a semantic rewrite or changes your input automatically.

faqs.question: Are index candidates verified?
faqs.answer: No. They are static hypotheses based on visible predicates and ordering, not verified recommendations from your schema or statistics.

faqs.question: Does an EXPLAIN finding prove a query is slow?
faqs.answer: No. The tool recognizes a small set of pasted plan tokens. Review the complete plan, estimates, data distribution, and workload in your database.

faqs.question: Will the suggestions make a query faster?
faqs.answer: There is no speed guarantee. Test any proposed change with the real schema, data, and representative workload.
